customer_question: We got SIG certification for another product a few years ago -- does that mean we're already a member? A search for our company name doesn't find a match.
question_variants: Why doesn't our company name show up in the member search?
Could we already be a member under a different company name?
Do we need new member registration, or are we already covered?
actual_issue: The customer believed their company might already be a Bluetooth SIG member based on a past certification, but a member search for the company name they provided ('Flight Solutions') returned no match, raising the question of whether new member registration was actually needed.
plain_english_explanation: Sometimes the name someone uses to introduce themselves in an email isn't the same as the official company name their organization is actually registered under with Bluetooth SIG -- this can happen when someone works across related companies or uses an informal name. Before concluding that a new membership needs to be set up, it's worth checking the history of how the conversation started, since the original contact may have come from a different, already-registered company name.
consultant_answer: A member search for 'Flight Solutions' (the name the customer's representative used) found no match. Reviewing the engagement's email history showed that the original contact for this matter actually came from a representative of 'Flight System Consulting Inc.,' on which the current representative (using the name 'Flight Solutions') had been CC'd. A member search for 'Flight System Consulting Inc.' found a match as an existing Adopter member. The customer was informed that if registering under the Flight System Consulting Inc. name was acceptable, no new member registration would be needed.
decision_logic: When a customer's stated company name does not match any Bluetooth SIG member search result, check the engagement's actual email history for an earlier-stated, differently-named entity the customer may be affiliated with, and search for that name as well, before concluding that new member registration is required.
final_recommendation: When a member search for a customer's stated company name fails, trace back through the engagement's email history for any earlier-stated, differently-named affiliated entity, and search for that name before assuming new member registration is needed.
risk_if_done_wrong: Assuming new member registration is required simply because the customer's stated company name doesn't match a search result, without checking for an affiliated entity name earlier in the engagement, could lead to unnecessary duplicate member registration.
search_aliases: company name not found in member search
check email history for affiliated company name
already a member under different company name
